title: Table 4 from rem:trivial-knot-photon-interpretation
html:
Term Product NF Interpretation
(13) \varphi_{01}V \cdot \mathbf{1} \varphi_{01}V = \varphi_{01}L_+ - \varphi_{01}h\,\sigma_0 The vertex passes through the core; unchanged.
(14) \varphi_{01}V \cdot \psi_0\sigma_0 \varphi_{01}\psi_0\bigl(e^- - h^2\sigma_0 - h\,\gamma\bigr) Vertex meets horizontal polarization: electron production. Via \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0 = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 - h\sigma_0^2 = e^- - h(h\sigma_0 + \mathbf{1}). The vertex of one photon combines with the horizontal crossing of the other to form the electron word e^-, with h-weighted vacuum and \sigma_0 remainders. This is the second of three mechanisms for electron production under \mathbf{1}.
(15) \varphi_{01}V \cdot \psi_1\sigma_1 \varphi_{01}\psi_1\sigma_0 Vertex meets vertical polarization. Via \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}\cdot\sigma_1 = \sigma_0: the vertical crossing cancels the vertex's inverse crossing exactly and the orthogonal polarization \sigma_0 is emitted, with no remainder. Compare term (8).
(16) \varphi_{01}V \cdot \psi_{01}V \varphi_{01}\psi_{01}\bigl(\sigma_1\sigma_0^{-1} - h^2V + h^2\gamma\bigr) = \varphi_{01}\psi_{01}\bigl(L_- - h\sigma_1 - h^2L_+ + h^3\sigma_0 + h^2\gamma\bigr) Two vertices collide. The self-product of the vertex produces the reversed vertex \sigma_1\sigma_0^{-1}, which carries L_-, together with an h^2-weighted vertex and vacuum. No electron channel opens here.
